neighbours.label: A body or person attribute noun (skin, hair, age) used as a classifier right before 'type(s)' or 'group': 'all skin types', 'every hair type', 'this age group'
fire: The new moisturiser was developed for all skin types, including sensitive ones.
Our stylists are trained to cut and colour all hair types and textures.
This sunscreen has been tested on every skin type under strong sunlight.
The conditioner works well on most hair types, even after bleaching.
The clinic runs a separate swimming class for each age group in the town.
Dermatologists recommend the serum for dry and oily skin types alike.
The salon sells brushes designed for different hair types and lengths.
Reading scores improved in every age group that took part in the trial.
quiet: The new moisturiser left her skin feeling smooth for the whole day.
Our stylists washed his hair twice before starting the cut.
Please choose the correct file type before saving the drawing.
The printer supports every paper type sold in the shop.
At her age, she still swims a mile before breakfast.
Dermatologists warn that the sun can damage skin within minutes.
The form asks for the account type and the branch number.
The salon closed early because the water had been cut off.

notes: Card: top examples 'all skin types', 'all hair types', 'cell lines'; the output direction of this pole promotes ' type'/' types'. Probes: skin types 0.60, hair type 0.56, age group 0.29, blood type 0.20, cell lines 0.13, file type 0.03; 'skin'/'cell' outside the classifier slot ~0.01. So the test uses skin, hair and age only; the wider 'any noun before type' reading did not hold in probing.
